nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: Since the Dawn Bell rang, the Guild Hall of Steady Steps has never been quiet. There is a queue for the stretching mats, a waiting list for the good kettle, and a sign in Maple's handwriting: PLEASE TAKE TURNS.

nodes.speaker: chad
nodes.text: {hero}! Come in, come in, mind the queue! I have been a guildmaster for years and I have never once had to say 'mind the queue'. I love it.

nodes.speaker: maple
nodes.text: He has said it forty times today. It has not worked once.

nodes.speaker: chad
nodes.text: Everyone came because of the bell. Some walked from the coast! Maple, tell {hero} about the coast.

nodes.speaker: maple
nodes.text: Hm. Fishing boats have been turning up since Tuesday. They say the harbour at Gullhaven is stuck. Fog on the water, and the lighthouse lamp has gone dark.

nodes.speaker: maple
nodes.text: All except one small lantern in the window. Somebody lights it every single night. Nobody knows who.

nodes.speaker: chad
nodes.text: The lantern from the end of last time! I have been wondering about it for weeks. I made a chart. It is mostly question marks.

nodes.speaker: biscuit
nodes.text: *Woof!*

nodes.speaker: chad
nodes.text: He says it is a good lantern. He has never seen it. He is a very trusting dog.

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: Somebody small is standing very still beside the notice board, holding a rolled-up mat in front of them like a shield.

nodes.speaker: chad
nodes.text: Ah, a newcomer! Step forward. Do not be alarmed, I only bite on Tuesdays.

nodes.speaker: maple
nodes.text: He does not bite.

nodes.speaker: chad
nodes.text: I am working on a reputation.

nodes.speaker: pip
nodes.text: Hi. I'm Pip. I heard the bell, and I thought maybe I could try. But everyone here looks like they know exactly what they're doing.

nodes.speaker: maple
nodes.text: Nobody knows exactly what they are doing. They have just been doing it for longer.

nodes.speaker: chad
nodes.text: {hero}! You were new here yourself not so long ago. Would you show Pip around?

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: Pip looks at you hopefully, then at the mat, then at the floor.

reply.speaker: pip
reply.text: Oh! There is a kettle? And a mat with a duck on it?

reply.speaker: chad
reply.text: The Duck Mat. Nobody knows why it has a duck. It is the best mat we own.

options.label: Share a snack and a seat.

reply.speaker: pip
reply.text: Thanks. I was not sure if I was allowed to sit down yet.

reply.speaker: maple
reply.text: You are allowed to sit down. Sitting down is in the rules. I wrote that rule.

options.label: Tell Pip you started small too.

reply.speaker: pip
reply.text: Really? You? ...Oh. That helps. That helps a lot.

reply.speaker: chad
reply.text: I did not start small! I started at Level 2. ...I started at Level 1, like everyone. Please carry on.

nodes.speaker: chad
nodes.text: Right! Pip, you are on the guild's books. That means you may take as long as you like, rest whenever you like, and nothing here has a deadline. Rest is training. I will keep saying so until somebody stops me.

nodes.speaker: pip
nodes.text: Okay. Okay. I think I can do that.

nodes.speaker: maple
nodes.text: The coast road is long. Somebody should go and see what is wrong with that lighthouse.

nodes.speaker: chad
nodes.text: And I would love to go, but a guildmaster cannot abandon his hall. Also my knees have filed a formal complaint.

nodes.speaker: chad
nodes.text: {hero}, would you go? At your own pace, with Biscuit and a bag of Maple's sandwiches?

nodes.speaker: pip
nodes.text: Can I come too? I am not very fast.

nodes.speaker: chad
nodes.text: Fast is something that happens to some people. Arriving is something that happens to everyone.

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: And so the Chronicle turns to a new page, and a road that leads west toward the sea.

nodes.speaker: maple
nodes.text: One flask. Two sandwiches each. A spare sock, because there is always a spare sock. And a map.

nodes.speaker: chad
nodes.text: I drew the map myself. It is mostly arrows. They are very confident arrows.

nodes.speaker: maple
nodes.text: Hm. They point in three directions.

nodes.speaker: chad
nodes.text: Confident in three directions! Go well, you two. If the road is long, sit down. If the road is lovely, sit down anyway.

nodes.speaker: brad
nodes.text: {hero}! Pip! I am your escort! I have scouted ahead. To that tree. And back. And to that tree again. The road is four hundred tree-lengths long.

nodes.speaker: brad
nodes.text: I have taken your advice, {hero}. I now rest on purpose. It is going very well. I have a schedule for it.

nodes.speaker: brad
nodes.text: Remember when you asked to join my rest? I kept your spot. I labelled it. It says RESERVED.

nodes.speaker: brad
nodes.text: You said my secret was safe, {hero}, and it has been. Nobody knows about my naps. Pip, do not ask about my naps.

nodes.speaker: pip
nodes.text: I did not ask.

nodes.speaker: brad
nodes.text: Good. Keep not asking.

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: A signpost stands at a fork in the road. It has eleven arrows. Ten of them say GULLHAVEN, and one says SORRY.

nodes.speaker: pip
nodes.text: I keep falling behind you both. I am sorry. You can go on ahead, honestly.

nodes.speaker: brad
nodes.text: Behind is a direction, Pip. It is not a verdict. I read that on a bookmark.

nodes.prompt: How do you walk the road?

reply.speaker: pip
reply.text: ...You do not mind? Oh. Then I will look at the view. I have not looked at a single view yet.

reply.speaker: brad
reply.text: I do this already! I call it a lap! Pip, you are my favourite finish line.

reply.speaker: pip
reply.text: Side by side. Nobody in front and nobody behind. I did not know that was an option.

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: Biscuit trots in loops around all three of them, which is, strictly speaking, a different pace again. Everybody allows it.

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: The road tops a rise, and the whole sea opens out below: wide, bright and rocking gently, as if it has all the time in the world.

nodes.speaker: pip
nodes.text: Oh. It is so big. And look, way over there on the cliff. Is that the lighthouse? It is so small.

nodes.speaker: brad
nodes.text: It is far. It is a bit farther than it looks. Everything worth reaching is. I read that too.

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: A tiny golden spark flickers in the tower, small and stubborn against the afternoon. Somebody is up there. Somebody is keeping it lit.

nodes.speaker: pip
nodes.text: I think I want to meet whoever that is.

chapters.title: The Slowest Ferry in the World

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: The road ends at a wide, golden river mouth. There is a wooden jetty, a flat-bottomed ferry, and a sign that says: FERRY. LEAVES WHEN IT LEAVES.

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: On the ferry sits a very old tortoise in a small red cap. He does not look up. He does not need to.

nodes.speaker: brad
nodes.text: Excellent! A ferry! When does it leave? I have been ready since the signpost.

nodes.speaker: sedge
nodes.text: ...Hello.

nodes.speaker: brad
nodes.text: Hello! When does it leave?

nodes.speaker: sedge
nodes.text: ...When it leaves.

nodes.speaker: pip
nodes.text: I like him already. He has not asked me to hurry once, and he has said four words.

nodes.speaker: sedge
nodes.text: Sedge. Ferry. ...Three hundred years. Never been late.

nodes.speaker: pip
nodes.text: Never once? How?

nodes.speaker: sedge
nodes.text: Never had... an appointment.

nodes.speaker: brad
nodes.text: That is either the wisest thing I have ever heard or the most annoying. I will let you know in a minute.

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: The ferry slides away from the jetty so gently that no one notices until the jetty is small. The river goes by in long, shining ripples.

nodes.speaker: brad
nodes.text: How long does this crossing take?

nodes.speaker: sedge
nodes.text: ...Longer than you would like. ...Shorter than you will remember.

nodes.prompt: How do you spend the crossing?

reply.speaker: sedge
reply.text: Good. ...Most of the river is only seen... by those who stop.

reply.speaker: sedge
reply.text: The keeper. Wren. ...Lights it every night. ...Has not crossed to rest in a long time.

options.label: Close your eyes for a while.

reply.speaker: narrator
reply.text: You doze to the sound of the river. Nobody wakes you.

reply.speaker: sedge
reply.text: The ferry will keep. ...It always does.

nodes.speaker: sedge
nodes.text: The big lamp. ...Its glass broke in the storm. Pieces fell. ...Into the harbour. Into the tide pools.

nodes.speaker: pip
nodes.text: So if we find the pieces, the lamp could shine again?

nodes.speaker: sedge
nodes.text: ...If someone... looks. Slowly. Carefully.

nodes.speaker: brad
nodes.text: I have counted four hundred ripples and I have not exploded. Pip, I think I am improving.

nodes.speaker: pip
nodes.text: You are doing really well, Brad.

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: At last the ferry noses into the far jetty. The sun has sunk a hand's width lower, and nobody can say exactly when.

nodes.speaker: sedge
nodes.text: Gullhaven is... a short walk. ...I will be here. ...I am always here.

nodes.speaker: pip
nodes.text: Thank you, Sedge. For not making me hurry.

nodes.speaker: sedge
nodes.text: Nobody... was ever made to hurry. ...By a river.

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: Brad opens his mouth to answer, closes it, and walks the first ten steps of the path at a perfectly reasonable speed.

chapters.title: The Keeper Who Forgot to Rest

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: Gullhaven harbour is full of boats and empty of sailors. They sit on upturned crates, looking out at the fog, listening for a sound they used to hear every morning.

nodes.speaker: grit
nodes.text: SURPRISE! I followed you! I was in Brad's backpack! It was very dark and it smelled of Brad!

nodes.speaker: brad
nodes.text: That is why my backpack was so heavy. I thought I was getting stronger.

nodes.speaker: grit
nodes.text: Remember the swap? I kept the shiny you gave me! It is my second-favourite shiny!

nodes.speaker: grit
nodes.text: You shared a snack with me! I have thought about that snack for months! Do you have another? ...Is that a trick? It is not a trick, is it?

nodes.speaker: grit
nodes.text: You asked me nicely, {hero}! Nobody asks nicely! It is the shiniest thing anyone has ever done!

nodes.speaker: grit
nodes.text: Anyway! I found something shiny in a fishing net! It is the best shiny yet! It is very sharp, so I am holding it by the very end!

nodes.speaker: pip
nodes.text: Grit, that is a piece of lamp glass! That is exactly what we are looking for!

nodes.speaker: grit
nodes.text: I KNEW it was good. I always know.

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: A figure comes along the quay in a navy coat and a yellow hat, carrying a lantern in front of her like something precious. She is walking the way people walk when they have forgotten how to stop.

nodes.speaker: wren
nodes.text: Visitors. Good. Hello. I cannot talk long. The lamp has to be lit every night, or somebody out there is lost.

nodes.speaker: pip
nodes.text: How many nights have you lit it?

nodes.speaker: wren
nodes.text: Forty-one. I think. It could be forty-three.

nodes.speaker: wren
nodes.text: I am Wren. Keeper of the Gullhaven light. I am fine. Fine is my whole job.

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: Her eyes close for just a moment, and she sways. Pip steps forward before anyone else can move.

nodes.speaker: wren
nodes.text: I am fine. The light cannot go out. I promised I would never let it go out.

nodes.prompt: What do you say to Wren?

options.label: Let us take the first watch.

reply.speaker: wren
reply.text: You would... You would mind it for me? Strangers? ...I do not know what to say.

options.label: Come and sit. I will make tea.

reply.speaker: wren
reply.text: Tea. I have not had tea sitting down since... I cannot remember. That is the answer, is it not?

options.label: The light can wait an hour.

reply.speaker: wren
reply.text: An hour. Just an hour. It sounds so small and so enormous at the same time.

nodes.speaker: wren
nodes.text: ...One hour. Please do not let the lantern go out.

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: Wren lies down on a coil of rope. In under a minute, she is asleep. The lantern, in Pip's careful hands, does not flicker once.

nodes.speaker: brad
nodes.text: I have never watched anything so important for so long. I am extremely good at it. Do not tell Chad.

nodes.speaker: pip
nodes.text: I think she needed someone to say it was allowed. Resting, I mean. She did not think it was.

nodes.speaker: grit
nodes.text: Is sleeping catching? I think I might be catching it. Is it normal to get sleepy when you are surrounded by shiny things?

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: An old sailor on a crate leans over to Pip and nods at the harbour wall. The tide goes out at dawn, he says. That is when the pools show what they are hiding.

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: At dawn the sea draws back and leaves the beach full of bright, shallow pools, each one a small, quiet world.

nodes.speaker: brad
nodes.text: Right. A plan! We search the beach in neat rows. Row one, row two, row three. Efficient. Methodical.

nodes.speaker: grit
nodes.text: I am searching in a spiral! Spirals are shinier!

nodes.speaker: biscuit
nodes.text: *Woof!*

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: Biscuit is not searching in rows or in a spiral. He is digging a hole. He appears to be enjoying himself more than anyone.

nodes.speaker: pip
nodes.text: Wait. Wait! There is something in this pool. Something glittering. I think... I found one. I actually found one!

nodes.speaker: brad
nodes.text: Technically I found the pool.

nodes.speaker: pip
nodes.text: Technically, yes! Thank you, Brad! Look at it. It has a rainbow in it!

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: On a rock at the edge of the beach, hugging a piece of driftwood, sits something small and purple, staring at the empty sand.

nodes.speaker: murmur
nodes.text: The sea went away. It went away, and I do not think it is coming back. What if tomorrow it does not come back? What if tomorrow is just... sand?

nodes.speaker: murmur
nodes.text: You said tomorrow was good too, {hero}. I have been practising saying it. 'Tomorrow is good too.' It is still a bit wobbly.

nodes.speaker: murmur
nodes.text: You said you would wait for me, {hero}. Nobody ever waits. I have been trying to be worth the wait. I am not sure how to start.

nodes.speaker: murmur
nodes.text: You asked me to walk with you, {hero}. I thought about it for a very long time. Then I walked. Here I am. A bit late.

nodes.speaker: pip
nodes.text: Hello, Murmur. I know that feeling. When everything goes away and you cannot see it coming back.

nodes.prompt: What do you tell Murmur about the tide?

options.label: It goes out every day, and comes back.

reply.speaker: murmur
reply.text: Every day? Even when I am not watching? ...That is very reliable of it.

options.label: Let's watch it come in together.

reply.speaker: murmur
reply.text: Together. I think I can be brave for a little while if it is together.

reply.speaker: murmur
reply.text: No rushing. The tide does not rush. It just... turns. I think I would like to turn, too.

nodes.speaker: grit
nodes.text: I have a shiny for sad times! It is a button! It is for you! It is a very good button!

nodes.speaker: murmur
nodes.text: ...It is a very good button. Thank you.

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: Slowly, so slowly that you only notice it by looking away and back, the water creeps in. It fills the channels, then the pools, then the sand.

nodes.speaker: murmur
nodes.text: It is coming back. Just like that. It did not even say it was sorry for leaving.

nodes.speaker: pip
nodes.text: The pools did not disappear, did they? They were just resting.

nodes.speaker: brad
nodes.text: That is the best thing I have heard all week. I would like it printed on a bookmark.

nodes.speaker: grit
nodes.text: I counted! Seven pieces of glass! Seven! It is a lot! It is basically a lamp already!

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: Murmur tucks the driftwood under one arm and, after a long breath, falls in with the others on the path toward the headland. Nobody asks them to hurry.

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: Wren is up and about, rested, and a little embarrassed. She has swept the whole lamp room twice, which she says is not working, just tidying.

nodes.speaker: wren
nodes.text: I slept eleven hours. I did not know I still could. Thank you. I mean it. I do not say it enough.

nodes.speaker: wren
nodes.text: Here is the trouble. We have the glass, and the glass is lovely. But the frame that held the great lens split in the storm, and it needs a long, straight beam of good timber.

nodes.speaker: grit
nodes.text: I know a place with lots of timber! It is an Oak Wood! There is a tree there who says 'hmph'!

nodes.speaker: wren
nodes.text: I promised my teacher I would never let the light go out. I heard 'never rest'. I think she meant 'never be alone with it'.

nodes.speaker: pip
nodes.text: That is a big difference.

nodes.speaker: wren
nodes.text: It is the whole difference.

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: A creaking cart appears on the headland road, pulled by a very patient pony. Sitting on the back is Maple, with a clipboard, and beside her a young sapling in a pot.

nodes.speaker: maple
nodes.text: Hm. Delivery. This is a branch. This is a letter. The letter took Oakhelm a whole season to write. I have not been allowed to hurry it.

nodes.speaker: maple
nodes.text: I will read it as written. It is slow. Sit down.

nodes.speaker: maple
nodes.text: 'Dear... {hero}. It is raining on me. This is nice.'

nodes.speaker: maple
nodes.text: 'I have heard about your lamp. I have enclosed a branch. It has been growing for forty years. I did not know it was for this. Neither did the branch.'

nodes.speaker: maple
nodes.text: 'You asked me about the best thing about being old. I have thought it over. It is the seasons coming back.'

nodes.speaker: maple
nodes.text: 'The squirrels have started writing again. They write in very small writing. I have not been able to read any of it. I do not mind.'

nodes.speaker: maple
nodes.text: 'You asked if you might sit a little longer. You may. The bench is yours. It has been yours since you asked.'

nodes.speaker: maple
nodes.text: 'Yours, Oakhelm. P.S. Hmph.'

reply.speaker: maple
reply.text: Hm. Short, warm, and no hurry. He will like that. I will carry it back slowly.

options.label: We will look after the branch.

reply.speaker: wren
reply.text: We will. I will carve the frame myself and keep a spare piece to remember it by.

reply.speaker: maple
reply.text: That, he will take literally. See you in about a year, {hero}. I will bring biscuits.

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: The whole afternoon goes into the frame. Wren carves, Maple measures, Pip holds the shards one by one against the light, and Grit presses a single shiny button into the very centre, for luck.

nodes.speaker: grit
nodes.text: It is not a mistake! It is a feature! It is a button feature!

nodes.speaker: wren
nodes.text: It is the best part of the lens. I thank you all. I forgot that a light is easier to keep when more than one person is looking after it.

nodes.speaker: maple
nodes.text: Hm. That is true of most things. Tea?

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: The great lens stands whole at last, patched with rainbow glass and a button. Tomorrow at dusk, the lamp will be lit.

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: Everyone camps at the foot of the tower, wrapped in blankets, with stars appearing one by one over the dark sea.

nodes.speaker: brad
nodes.text: Tomorrow I will carry the lamp oil up all one hundred and eighty-two steps. Without stopping. With enthusiasm.

nodes.speaker: wren
nodes.text: You will stop at every landing.

nodes.speaker: brad
nodes.text: ...I will stop at every landing, with enthusiasm.

nodes.speaker: murmur
nodes.text: I counted the stars. There were more than yesterday. Tomorrow will have even more. I am almost looking forward to it.

nodes.speaker: grit
nodes.text: I counted my shinies! There were exactly the same! I checked three times! That is also good!

nodes.speaker: wren
nodes.text: I have never lit this lamp with anyone beside me. Do you know what it is like to look up and see everyone here? It is a bit like being a tide.

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: Later, when the others are quiet, Pip sits on the edge of the rocks beside you, knees pulled up to their chin.

nodes.speaker: pip
nodes.text: Can I tell you something? I am really scared about the stairs.

nodes.speaker: pip
nodes.text: A hundred and eighty-two. What if I get to the middle and cannot go on? What if everyone has to wait for me, and I ruin the whole night?

reply.speaker: pip
reply.text: That is a funny thing to say. But it feels... true? Like it counts, even the small, silly versions.

reply.speaker: pip
reply.text: Every landing. There are nine. That is ten small climbs instead of one enormous one. ...I can do ten small ones.

reply.speaker: pip
reply.text: Beside me. Not behind and not in front. ...Okay. I think I just got a bit taller.

nodes.speaker: pip
nodes.text: Thank you. I know I did not start well. But I am glad I came.

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: From the dark, a grumbling, familiar voice: "Nobody ruins anything by being slow. Slow is how everything gets done."

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: A wheezing shape comes up the headland path, leaning on a very large walking stick and carrying a very small bag.

nodes.speaker: pip
nodes.text: Chad?! You came!

nodes.speaker: chad
nodes.text: I walked. All the way. It took four days. I rested at step eleven every single morning, and I saw a goose do something unspeakable.

nodes.speaker: brad
nodes.text: You walked? Alone? All that way?

nodes.speaker: chad
nodes.text: I was not alone. I had my dignity. It was mostly a hindrance.

nodes.speaker: chad
nodes.text: Maple said the hall can run itself for a week. She wrote it down and made me sign it, in front of witnesses. And, {hero}, I wanted to see the light. I wanted to see my guild.

nodes.speaker: wren
nodes.text: You must be Chad. I heard you rang a bell. I have been waiting a long time to meet whoever did.

nodes.speaker: chad
nodes.text: Oh, I did not ring it. Everyone did. That is what a guild is. ...Please. Is there anywhere to sit?

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: Everyone shuffles up on a single blanket. Biscuit, who has been awake the whole time, politely pretends to be asleep.

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: At dusk, they climb. All one hundred and eighty-two steps, and nine landings, and a good many pauses. Chad rests at step eleven. Brad rests at step twelve, purely to support him.

nodes.speaker: pip
nodes.text: Three more landings. I am doing it. I am actually doing it! Do not look at me, I might get nervous.

nodes.speaker: grit
nodes.text: I am looking at the buttons on the stairs! There are no buttons on the stairs! I am looking anyway!

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: At the top, the great lens waits in the lamp room, whole, patched with rainbow glass and one shiny button. Beyond it, the sea turns the colour of a ripe peach.

nodes.speaker: wren
nodes.text: Forty-one nights I lit the little lantern alone. Tonight, someone else should light the great lamp. {hero}, will you?

nodes.prompt: How do you light the lamp?

reply.speaker: narrator
reply.text: You strike a single spark, patient and steady. The wick takes it, and the flame grows, and grows.

reply.speaker: narrator
reply.text: Wren holds the wick, Pip the lamp, Brad the oil, Chad the spark, and Grit the button. It is not tidy. The flame catches anyway.

reply.speaker: pip
reply.text: Me? ...Okay. Okay! I think I can. Just... hold my hand a second.

reply.speaker: narrator
reply.text: Pip's spark is small and a little shaky. It is exactly enough.

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: The great lamp wakes. Light pours through the patched lens, a hundred small rainbows at once, and a single bright beam sweeps out over the water.

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: Out at sea, one by one, small lanterns blink awake on the water. The fleet has been waiting, and now it is coming home.

nodes.speaker: murmur
nodes.text: Look at them all. They found the way. I did not think they would. ...I am very glad I was wrong.

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: And then, far off to the east, so faint that everyone has to hold their breath, a deep, warm note rolls across the dark: BONG.

nodes.speaker: wren
nodes.text: That is the bell. Your Dawn Bell. Somebody is ringing it, back in the valley. It is answering the light.

nodes.speaker: chad
nodes.text: Maple. She must have climbed the tower herself. Without telling me. On her day off. ...Dawn Bell by morning, lantern by night. Someone to say hello at both ends of the day.

nodes.speaker: brad
nodes.text: I would like it noted that I carried the oil, rested at every landing, and did not explode.

nodes.speaker: pip
nodes.text: It is noted, Brad.

nodes.speaker: wren
nodes.text: Now. If nobody minds, I am going to bed. A real bed, with a pillow. For ten hours. And tomorrow the lamp will be looked after by the whole of Gullhaven, in shifts.

nodes.speaker: chad
nodes.text: Rest is training, Wren. It is on a banner. I will send you the banner.

nodes.speaker: chad
nodes.text: Come by when you like, {hero}. Move however you like. Rest when you need to. The hall is yours.

nodes.speaker: chad
nodes.text: Come by when you like, {hero}. Have fun with it, the way you said you would. The hall is yours.

nodes.speaker: chad
nodes.text: Come by when you like, {hero}. Stay curious, the way you did from the very first day. The hall is yours.

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: The beam sweeps the sea, the bell answers from the hills, and a place is kept at the Guild Hall for whoever walks in next. The lamp burns on, and everyone sleeps at their own pace.
